story_text.value:
Sill (discussed here: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50112739) streams one Mac window, or the whole Desktop, to an iPhone or iPad and lets you control it by touch. It's open source, so I made an Android client for it. It's unofficial and not affiliated with Sill's author: it speaks Sill's existing protocol, so the Mac side is the stock Sill app, unchanged.

Install Sill on the Mac, sideload the APK from Releases onto an Android 11+ phone on the same Wi-Fi, tap your Mac in the list that shows on your phone, then look for the 12-digit code in Sill on your Mac, and type it into the Android app.

Then: tap to click, drag to scroll, hold-and-drag to select text or move windows, pinch to zoom the picture on the phone, a Draw toggle for whiteboard apps like tldraw, and a key row with Esc, Tab, Cmd/Ctrl/Option/Shift and arrows. It also works over Tailscale with Sill's Remote Access.

All of the code was written by Claude Code, working from Sill's Swift source and its Python test client; I tested it on a Pixel 9 Pro XL.

Not done yet: drawing the Mac's pointer, a trackpad mode, clipboard sync, and a Play Store listing (I don't have Play developer account, and new individual Play developer accounts can't publish their first app until they've tested an app with a closed test with 12 testers.)

story_text.value:
Hi HN,

I've been through many finance tracking apps, starting with Personal Capital, then Monarch, and most recently Copilot. None of them have worked perfectly for my needs.

All of these apps tend to model “cash flow” as the net sum of your transactions during a month, yet while credit card charges are reported immediately, they are typically deducted from checking (cash) accounts the following month when the bill is due. As a result, I've always had to maintain a separate spreadsheet to track my actual cash flow.

These apps also have a huge focus on managing budgets, which has never been for me. My spending is rarely consistent month-to-month, so every month I'm comparing my fully justified spending against my budget, and tweaking my budget until I “pass”.

So I built yet another finance tracking app. It has the usual components - accounts, transactions, categories - but the core is a cash flow projection engine, and everything else is built around it.

Budgets are gone. Instead, each income/spending category is projected forward from your historical activity, but not as a flat monthly number. They land in whatever account you historically use (e.g. checking account for paychecks/rent/bills, credit/debit cards for daily spending). Credit card payments are modeled automatically based on your projected credit card balance. You can set up your own recurring transfers between accounts as well, to model savings, for example.

The end result is that the app can forecast how your cash moves, and you can see in advance when any account might run low. If all of your accounts look good for the next 12 months, maybe you don't have a budgeting problem.

What’s made the biggest difference for me has been the MCP integration, which I have connected to Claude (but can be connected to any AI agent of your choice). I have asked it to import historical transactions by uploading PDF account statements, categorize/tag all transactions that took place while I was on vacation, and plan transfers across my accounts to cover expected payments.

I hope some people that share my frustrations will find this app useful.

story_text.value:
My Downloads folder is full of files like download (3).pdf, IMG_4821.jpg, and Untitled.docx. I already have folders for them in Documents. I never move them because I have to open each file to know what it is. Putaway does that part.

It reads the start of each file on your Mac: PDF text, OCR for scans and photos, Word, Excel, CSV, and HTML. Then it picks one of the folders you already have. It never makes new folders. It shows you the plan first. Nothing moves until you click Move, and Undo puts everything back.

Demo (this run uses a SubQ key, so some files are ready to move): https://github.com/devYRPauli/putaway/blob/main/docs/demo.gi...

You choose the model. The default is Apple Intelligence on your Mac. It is free, and nothing leaves your Mac. You can also use your own model through any OpenAI-compatible server, such as Ollama or LM Studio. Or you can add your own SubQ or Jev API key. Those two give a probability for each folder, so Putaway moves the files they are sure about. With Apple or your own model, you confirm each file.

I tested the released build on 107 files with messy names: public IRS forms, papers, receipts, photos, and spreadsheets, plus fake secret files and a partial download. There were 19 target folders, including decoy folders that apps make, such as Zoom and Adobe. Files in an acceptable folder: SubQ 88%, Jev 85%, qwen2.5 7B in Ollama 82%, Apple's on-device model 67% (of the 99 files it agreed to read). When SubQ or Jev moved a file on its own, it was right 132 of 136 times.

One surprise: Apple's on-device model refused to read three blank government forms, including the IRS 1040, as unsafe content. Putaway leaves those files in place and tells you why.

It never reads files with names like .env, id_rsa, or recovery-codes.txt. If a file's text looks like a private key or a token, it does not send it. It never overwrites a file, and it skips downloads that are not complete.

Install (Apple Silicon, macOS 26). The install script is 33 lines, so you can read it first:

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/devYRPauli/putaway/main/install.sh | bash

  brew install devyrpauli/tap/putaway
It is a Swift menu bar app and a CLI, MIT-licensed, with no dependencies. I do not pay for an Apple developer account, so the app is not notarized. The curl and brew installs do not show the Gatekeeper prompt.

I want to know which files it puts in the wrong folder, and which file types it misses. Keynote, Pages, and pptx files are filed by name only for now.

story_text.value:
EtherPK now has Agent Chat.

I use AI agents in two distinct ways. For coding I use TUIs, but for day-to-day and non code projects I used to use the web chat UIs like many others. Two things about this was always jarring:

You're starting context from scratch. You might have a couple of agent instructions configured, but you have to tell the agent what you're thinking, from the beginning. When you get the information you need, holding on to it is hard. Within a day or two it's burried in your chat history. EtherPK is a mardown based PKMS (notes app), and it solves both of these problems.

You can type /Agent within your notes (EtherPK supports standard prose and outliner blocks in the same document). The Agent Chat panel opens within your document, and you can choose how much context to give it. That might be nothing, the current block tree, the document or the whole graph (in the case of the latter - immediate surounding context is sent and the agent is given tools to navigate the rest of your graph). You control what the agent gets, and what stays private.

title.value: Show HN: Agent Chat in Your Markdown Notes – Chat with Context and Save Response

story_text.value:
Hi everyone! I'm Joe, and I built Tennis: a CLI that indexes and searches your context offline. You can index any files, your Chat & Claude sessions, Codex history, etc. All local and offline.

I've always hated having chats siloed in Claude and not having an easy way to connect that context in other apps. Anything that exists today has a subscription and is stored on their servers, and really wanted something fast, local, and offline.

How Tennis works: * SQLite/FTS5 (keyword) + vec0 (vector) * model2vec / potion-retrieval-32M (512-dim, 123MB). This is a flat vector table, and what helps make this work well local/offline. * RRF (k=60) fuses BM25 keyword rank + cosine semantic rank into one score

Tennis also creates markdown files called 'cards' at indexing time. This gives you an easy, summarized, human readable format to see what Tennis has. You can edit these files (but won't change the embeddings in SQLite).

You can use Tennis via API and MCP. It's incredibly fast, and the MCP works great as a connector to different applications (ChatGPT, Claude, Opencode, etc).

You can install and use it today: https://tennis.jlachance1.workers.dev/

Thanks for checking this out! I would love any feedback. Thank you
